Title: Source 2: [Adapted from] Poverty (1905)
Content: `text(Millions)` of foreigners established neighborhoods in the very hearts of our urban and industrial communities. `text(Two)` groups have generally promoted immigration: large employers seeking the cheapest form of labor obtainable, and the owners of the transatlantic steamship companies. These agencies made the people believe fabulous stories of wealth to be had in America... In `text(one)` community where I lived, several `text(thousand)` human beings were struggling fiercely against want. Fully `text(fifty thousand)` men, women, and children were all the time either in poverty or on the verge of poverty. They worked and starved and ached to rise out of it. They broke their health down. The men acquired painful and disabling diseases. The girls and boys followed in the paths of their parents. The wages were so low that the men alone often could not support their families. Mothers with babies toiled in order to add to the income. They gave up all thought of joyful living.
